senses.definition: A word, symbol, or phrase used to identify a particular company's product and differentiate it from other companies' products.

subsenses.definition: Especially, such a term that is registered with a government agency so as to have legal protection against use by other companies.

senses.definition: Any proprietary business, product or service name.

quotes.text: Trademark Notice / The following are trademarks or registered trademarks of their respective companies: […] Google is a trademark of Google Corporation; eBay is a trademark of eBay, Inc.
quotes.reference: 2005, Kai A. Olsen, The Internet, the Web, and eBusiness, page xv:

senses.definition: The aspect for which someone or something is best known; a hallmark or typical characteristic.
(transitive, proscribed) To register something as a trademark.
(transitive, proscribed) To so label a product.

quotes.text: Sutho took a pull at his Johnny Walker and Coke and laughed that trademark laugh of his and said: `Okay. I'll pay that all right.'
quotes.reference: 1996, Jon Byrell, Lairs, Urgers and Coat-Tuggers, Sydney: Ironbark, page 294:

quotes.text: Riise did crash a fantastic, trademark free-kick against the bar from 25 yards but it was the Potters who increasingly posed the greater threat.
quotes.reference: 2011 October 15, Owen Phillips, “Stoke 2 - 0 Fulham”, in BBC Sport:

quotes.text: The world’s most powerful man entered with an air of unhurried bonhomie. Dressed in his trademark navy suit and red tie, Trump, 78, appeared a little older than he had some seven months earlier, when he last met with TIME—more subdued, less verbose, the same discursive speech patterns but with the volume turned down.
